calls.reason: The claim is universal, and the packet has counterexamples. Palantir, an AI-software company, reported $871M GAAP net income for Q1 2026, and Gamma's CEO said it reached $100M ARR profitably.

No one has independently checked the internal documents he cites, and no record shows a deliberate choice not to disclose. Microsoft's public $37B run-rate figure neither confirms nor refutes his claim.

Epoch AI's estimates for late 2025 put OpenAI and Anthropic well below half of the world's AI compute, and below half even among the five leading labs. That is far under 70% on the compute half of the claim.

In Q1 2026 filings, operating income at Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta grew by billions after depreciation. For Alphabet and Meta, the operating-income gain was several times the rise in depreciation.
Bloomberg estimates OpenAI at about 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue, which fits the first part. But the 80% compute share is unverified, and OpenAI's full-year 2026 loss is not yet known.

"Barely any" demand at a scale that "substantiates" the spending has no measurable threshold. The packet has Copilot seat counts and Google's AI growth rates, but no total of demand excluding OpenAI and Anthropic to compare with the capex.
